RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Thursday,  the December 14, 2006/Agrahayana 23, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Prime Minister; Atomic Energy; Coal; Communications and
Information Technology; Development of North-Eastern Region; External
Affairs; Housing and Urban Poverty Alleviation; Information and
Broadcasting; Overseas Indian Affairs; Panchayati Raj;
Parliamentary Affairs; Personnel, Public Grievances
and Pensions; Planning; Shipping, Road Transport
and Highways; Space; Statistics and Programme
Implementation; Urban Development;
Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Non-functioning of telephones under
Jaisinghpur telephone exchange
*321. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will
the Minister of COMMUNICATIONS
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
many telephones under Jaisinghpur
telephone exchange in Kangra district of
Himachal Pradesh remain out of order for
most of the time;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government in this behalf;
(c) whether Government have taken
any note not to charge rent for such period
from the subscribers of such telephones;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not
the reasons therefor?
Expansion of Urdu channel
†*322. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
Will the Minister of INFORMATION
AND BROADCASTING  be pleased to
state:
(a) the efforts being made by
Government to expand Urdu channel;
(b) the number of people who have been
given employment in it;
(c) whether Urdu channel is not
available in Urdu speaking regions; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor?
NOC for allotment of Lignite Blocks
*323. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased
to state:
(a) the reasons for which 'No Objection

101
Certificate' is required from Neyveli Lignite
Corporation (NLC) for allotment of Lignite
Block when, NLC is also a mining company
and restricted to Tamil Nadu  State only;
(b) whether Government have any plan
to withdraw this NOC system; and
(c) if so, by when?
Allowing of small shops in residential
areas
*324. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact  that Government
have given wide publicity in leading
newspapers of NCT  of  Delhi through
advertisements on the 12th  of October, 2006
allowing small shops in residential  areas in
22 categories of trades in compliance with
the orders of Hon'ble Supreme  Court;
(b) if so, the complete details of the
scheme formulated by Government;
(c) whether Government have allowed
only one shop on one plot, irrespective of
plot area; and
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and the
steps being taken to allow more traders on
bigger plots?
Animals dying on a NH in accidents
†*325. MISS ANUSUIYA UIKEY: Will
the Minister of  SHIPPING, ROAD
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether animals die due to accidents
with vehicles passing through Pench
National Park on National Highway
touching Nagpur, Sivni and Jabalpur;
(b) if so, the number of animals that
died in such accidents during the last five
years;
(c) the efforts being  made to prevent
occurrence of such deaths of animals due
to accidents; and
(d) whether the proposal of diverting
this route is under consideration; if so; the
place of such diversion and the status
thereof?
NHs in Bihar
†*326. SHRI SHATRUGHAN
SINHA: Will the Minister of SHIPPING,
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS
be pleased to state:
(a) the total length of National
Highways in Bihar State;
(b) the  stretch therefrom where four-
lane  conversion work has been going on
under "Golden Quadrilateral" and East-
West Corridor project;
(c) the status of the remaining  length of
National Highways;
(d) whether State Government has
demanded Centre's help to improve
condition of these Highways; and
(e) if so, the action being taken by the
Central Government in this regard?
Accidents in the coal mine of
Dhanbad
*327. DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA :
Will the PRIME MINISTER  be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have taken
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

102
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
steps for the expeditious and
comprehensive investigations into the
recent accident in the coal mine in Dhanbad
district; if so, the details thereof;
(b) whether the report has been
submitted and if not, the reasons therefor;
(c) what are  the findings of the
investigations and whether they reveal the
omissions and commissions of the
concerned officers;
(d) whether the investigations also
revealed on what counts the Mine Safety
Standards were violated;
(e) whether the investigations have
looked into the conduct of rescue work; and
(f) whether the district has adequate
infrastructure to undertake the rescue work?

SHRI C. PERUMAL:

Atomic energy plant in Madhya
Pradesh
†2414. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH :
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government of Madhya
Pradesh has submitted a proposal for
atomic power house of 2000 MW;
(b) if so, by when the said proposal
would be approved; and
(c) the reasons for not according
priority to it despite the severe shortage of
power in Madhya Pradesh?
Construction of nuclear energy plants
by private sector
2415. MS. MABEL REBELLO : Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the private sector would be
allowed to construct nuclear energy plants
in India;
(b) if so, how the Department would
process to allocate nuclear plants to private
sector in India in details;
(c) whether his Ministry would allow
private sector overseas to come and build
these nuclear plants in India;
(d) if so, the detials thereof; if not the
reasons therefor; and
(c) the total potential of nuclear energy
plants Government propose to construct
within the next 5-10 years?
Movement by displaced persons in
Talcher field, Orissa
†2416. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the PRIME MINISTER be
pleased to state:
(a) the measures being taken to resolve
the ongoing movement by the displaced
persons in the Talcher field under Mahanadi
Coalfields Limited (M.C.L.) situated in
Orissa;

551
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) the reasons for not providing the
required employment to the displaced
persons therefor; and
(c) the extent of employment provided
in other fields in comparison to the
production and it's statistics in Talcher field?
Rate of coal royalty
2417. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) what is Government's view on the
report submitted on 14th July 2006, by
the Committee constituted for revision of
rates of royalty;
(b) whether Government is agreeable to
royalty fixed on market rates as suggested
by Planning Commission and requested by
Chhattisgarh Government which obtains
78 per cent of its royalty revenue from
coal; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Report by the Chief Vigilance Officer,
CIL
†2418. SHRI RAMADHAR
KASHYAP: Will the PRIME MINISTER
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Chief Vigilance Officer of
CIL had concluded in his report that "such
companies exist only on papers which were
allotted the work of coal transportation in
Dipika and Gevra coal mines under SECL
(Chhattisgarh) and a special group has
ownership rights of these companies;
(b) whether it has also been indicated in
the said report that SECL has handed over its
complete control rights to the said group; and
(c) if so, the action taken by SECL
against the said coal transportation
company?
Assessment of coal reserves in
Jharkhand
2419. SHRI S. S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether extractable coal reserves
falling within Jharkhand has been assessed;
(b) if so, the details including findings
thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor;
(d) the details of the existing industrial
demands for coking and non-coking coal in
Jharkhand being met by Coal India and/or
its subsidiaries out of the coal mined in the
State itself and from outside the State both
in absolute and in percentage terms; and
(e) whether coal demands of industries
in Jharkhand are being met by mines in
other States and, at the same time, coal
mined within Jharkhand being exported to
other States, justification thereof?
Guidelines for issuing permits
†2420. DR. PRABHA THAKUR : Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) the guidelines and rules/regulations
fixed by the Central Government for issuing
permits to public and private sector
industries and organizations;
(b) the rate per metric tonne in rupees
fixed for the coal extracted so far in the
current financial year;
(c) the company-wise details of the
complaints/information received against the
coal permits issued in contravention of
guidelines and rules/regulations as on date;
and
(d) the action taken so far in this regard?

552
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Revision of coal royalty rates
†2421. SHRI SURENDRA LATH: Will
the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that royalty for
mining coal has not been revised for the
last five years;
(b) whether it is also a fact
